chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Ji'abi informed me, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda narrated to us that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya narrated to them, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Badr narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Yazid ibn Murra, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

"There is no servant who is attentive to the timings of the prayers and the positions of the sun except that I guarantee for him comfort at the time of death, the cessation of worries and sorrows, and salvation from the Fire."
We were once herders of camels, and now today we are herders of the sun.

key_terms.الروح: comfort and ease of the soul
key_terms.رعاة الشمس: herders/minders of the sun — a metaphor for those who track the sun for prayer times
key_terms.مواضع الشمس: the positions of the sun used to determine prayer times
key_terms.مواقيت الصلاة: the designated times of the five daily prayers

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about observing prayer times and watching the sun?
ai.summary: The Prophet (saw) emphasizes the spiritual rewards of carefully observing prayer times by tracking the sun's position, promising comfort at death, freedom from worry, and salvation from Hellfire. The closing remark reflects the transformation of the early Muslim community from a pastoral society to one devoted to precise prayer timing, showing how worship became their primary occupation and concern.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 5. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Ja'abi told me: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda narrated to us that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya narrated to them, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Badr narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Yazid ibn Murra, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) that the Holy Prophet (saw) said:

"There is no servant who is concerned with the timings of the prayers and the positions of the sun except that he is guaranteed comfort at the time of death, relief from worries and sorrows, and salvation from the Fire."
(The narrator said): "Sometimes back, we were minding the camels, now we mind the sun."
